cards.explanation: The answer is that same day. Haggai 2:20 says it's "For the second time that day…" on the twenty-fourth day of the month. Haggai, a prophet (Haggai 2:1), gets two words from the LORD in one day. I'd be tired just carrying the mail, friends.

The answer is the heavens and the earth. The LORD says, "…I am about to shake the heavens and the earth…" (Haggai 2:21) He's not talking about one wall or one field, friends. That's the whole kitchen AND the whole planet.

The answer is False. The LORD says, "I will overturn royal thrones and destroy the power of the kingdoms of the nations." (Haggai 2:22) He doesn't protect them, He overturns them. Big thrones, bigger flip.

The answer is True, there's a second part. The LORD says, "I will overturn royal thrones and destroy the power of the kingdoms of the nations." (Haggai 2:22) Thrones go over, and the kingdoms' power goes down with them. It's a two-part promise, friends.

The answer is his brother's sword. The LORD says, "horses and their riders will fall, each by the sword of his brother." (Haggai 2:22) Each rider falls by the sword of his own brother. That's what the text says, friends, so I'll leave it right there.

The word is servant. The LORD says, "…I will take you, My servant, Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel…" (Haggai 2:23) Zerubbabel is the governor, but the LORD calls him "My servant." I'd frame that title and hang it by the oven, bakers.

The answer is His signet ring. The LORD says, "…I will make you like My signet ring…" (Haggai 2:23) A signet ring is the kind of thing that stamps a seal. As a stamper myself, I take that one a little personally, in the best way.
The word is chosen. The LORD says, "…for I have chosen you…" (Haggai 2:23) The text gives that as the reason for the signet ring. Chosen, plain and simple, friends.
